title: New episode — three-shot workflow template
brief: Replace with the story or activity, audience, intended result and tone. Begin with a few examples to validate the workflow.
look: Replace with the intended visual treatment. Use actual character/style images as visual inputs in manual image-app handoffs.
continuity: Record established appearance, recurring props and camera convention. Label unknowns and new proposals explicitly.
episode_notes: Episode > scenes > shots. Human selection of composition, finished starter and final clip. Keep local drawing prompts visual and concise. One clear physical beat per initial clip test.

shots.title: Establish the starting situation
shots.purpose: Make the setting and starting state clear.
shots.composition: Define subject placement, important objects and the camera view.
shots.start_state: Define what is visible before any action.
shots.camera: Choose a fixed view or one simple camera movement.
shots.end_state: Define the physical state at the cut.
shots.feedback: Review staging before enhancement; attach actual appearance references.

shots.title: One readable action
shots.purpose: Test the complete image-to-clip workflow with this shot.
shots.start_state: Continue from the preceding physical state.
shots.action: Specify a feasible start, movement and finish.
shots.camera: Keep subject motion separate from camera motion.

shots.title: Show the result
shots.purpose: Confirm cause, continuity and the intended story outcome.
shots.start_state: Preserve the previous shot's objects and positions.
shots.action: A small reaction or held result.
